response.why: Missing our land drop (pass, or casting Preacher without playing land) delays Sheoldred, the Apocalypse — with 4 lands after either land drop we can hard-cast Sheoldred next priority window (Darkslick's flexibility covers the double-black either way), which is far stronger than a Preacher on an empty opposing board. Playing a land keeps that plan on track; the case where they resolve their own Sheoldred is the one board state that concerns me and pushes toward reactive Enduring Curiosity as a blocker.
response.plan: Play a land now, then cast Sheoldred, the Apocalypse with all 4 mana this main phase — the board is empty of real blockers for them. Hold Enduring Curiosity and Preacher of the Schism for follow-up turns.

response.why: Holding Floodpits Drowner (pass) lets us stun whatever threat actually matters once we see it — stunning Sheoldred before it can attack (leaves 0/1/3/4) locks it down through their whole next turn and is clearly the best line, especially against the weaker Preacher line (3/4) since their board stays thinner. Doing nothing (2/5) leaves Sheoldred free to swing with deathtouch, which is dangerous even with chump blockers available. Casting Floodpits Drowner blind right now (6-8) sometimes whiffs on stopping Sheoldred and in leaf 6 risks eating a double deathtouch attack (Sheoldred + animated Restless Reef) for up to 8 unless we chump both.
response.plan: Pass and hold Floodpits Drowner with flash + open mana through their turn. If Sheoldred is about to attack or a scary new threat (Kaito/Preacher/animated Restless Reef) resolves, flash in Floodpits Drowner to tap+stun the biggest threat before combat damage. Otherwise proceed to our postcombat main to play Restless Reef as our land drop and keep Spyglass Siren + both Vampire Tokens as chump blockers.

response.why: In every branch, using Floodpits Drowner to tap+stun Sheoldred (leaving it dead through their whole next turn) is clearly correct — those leaves (0,1,3,4,6,8,9,10) all score well above the 'do nothing' leaves (2,5,7) where Sheoldred stays live and can smash for 4 deathtouch damage. Worst case is leaf 5: we hold up mana but don't act, so Sheoldred stays free AND their own Floodpits Drowner resolves unopposed, stunning one of our blockers while adding a 2/1 body. Best case is leaf 6, where Sheoldred gets locked down and their follow-up (Anoint with Affliction) adds no real board threat. Leaf 4 is slightly worse than leaf 3 because waiting for their Drowner to fully resolve lets its ETB stun one of our creatures before we can stop it.
response.plan: Pass and hold Floodpits Drowner up with flash + mana open. Respond immediately (on the stack, before their spell resolves) if they cast anything with a relevant ETB (like their own Floodpits Drowner) so we lock Sheoldred before they can stun one of ours; otherwise stun Sheoldred as soon as it's clearly not going to get a better target. Then move to postcombat main to play Restless Reef and hold Spyglass Siren + both Vampire Tokens back as blockers.

Passing leaves Sheoldred fully untapped and able to swing for 4 deathtouch damage this turn, which at our 8 life is a serious risk.

This denies their best attacker for this turn and their next, buying us time to stabilize with Spyglass Siren, the two Vampire Tokens, and our own Preachers next turn. Keep Restless Reef in hand for our land drop.

Not attacking at all (leaf 0) wastes a great opportunity.
response.plan: Attack with everything: Preacher of the Schism, Spyglass Siren, and both Vampire Tokens. This should kill their only blocker, push them to low life, gain us life back via lifelink, and draw extra cards off Enduring Curiosity. Reassess blockers next turn based on what they develop.

response.why: Kaito's -2 ability (tap target creature, put two stun counters on it) targeting their Enduring Curiosity is clearly the best play available this turn — it neutralizes their only real threat for two of their turns, matching how effectively we locked down Sheoldred earlier. Those leaves (55-63) score highest, especially the clean 'do nothing' follow-ups. Cut Down still can't touch Enduring Curiosity (7) or Kaito (7), so firing it there (on stack or resolved) is wasted across most branches; it only earns real value against small things like Floodpits Drowner (leaves 33-34, killed cleanly) or Spyglass Siren (leaves 41-42). Playing a land instead of using -2 (the Restless Reef/Island candidates) is fine but strictly worse since it forfeits the free removal-like effect on their biggest body.
response.plan: Use Kaito's -2 ability to tap and put two stun counters on Enduring Curiosity, locking it down for two turns. Hold both Cut Down copies for a legitimately small target (Floodpits Drowner, Deep-Cavern Bat, Spyglass Siren, Faerie Mastermind). Play our land drop (Restless Reef or Island) afterward.

The clear high-value plays are killing Deep-Cavern Bat (2) or Spyglass Siren (2) once they actually resolve (leaves 5-6, 25, 33-34, 38-39), and casting our own Enduring Curiosity reactively for card advantage when we have spare mana instead of wasting a blind Cut Down (leaves 11, 14, 17, 20, 28) is solid value. response.plan: Hold both Cut Down copies for real small targets (Deep-Cavern Bat, Spyglass Siren, Floodpits Drowner, Faerie Mastermind). If mana is otherwise idle, flash in Enduring Curiosity for card advantage rather than wasting Cut Down on something too big.

response.why: Opponent is at 1 life with no legal blockers (their only creature is tapped and, even if new creatures resolve mid-turn, they're either summoning sick non-blockers or a Kaito that isn't a creature outside its controller's own turn), and we have three redundant lethal threats (Preacher, Vampire Token, Kaito) plus Restless Reef as a backup attacker - so we win this turn almost regardless of what we do. The only real differentiators are: (1) never cast Cut Down at a target with total P+T>5 (Preacher 6, Enduring Curiosity 7, Kaito 7, Sheoldred 9, animated Restless Reef 8 are all illegal) or at a spell still on the stack (no permanent to target yet) - these are wasted/illegal and scored low; (2) proactively casting Cut Down or Anoint with Affliction as our own main-phase play right now has no good legal target except our own Vampire Token/Preacher, so those root lines are misplays and scored low even though we still win; (3) Go for the Throat can legally and safely snipe opponent's Enduring Curiosity anytime since it's unconditional; (4) letting small real threats (Deep-Cavern Bat, Spyglass Siren, Faerie Mastermind) resolve and then Cut Down them post-resolution is clean value; (5) casting a second legendary Kaito forces the legend rule with no upside - low value; (6) Kaito's loyalty abilities are free (don't tap him, he can still attack) so mildly positive but largely irrelevant since the game is already won.
response.plan: Prefer passing/holding everything and using instant-speed responses only for clean, legal kills (Go for the Throat on their Enduring Curiosity, or Cut Down on genuinely small post-resolution targets); avoid wasting removal on illegal/oversized targets or on our own creatures. Proceed to combat and swing with Preacher, Vampire Token, and Kaito for lethal - opponent has no blockers available.

response.why: Same overwhelming position as last turn (opponent 1 life, empty hand, no legal blockers, we hold three redundant lethal threats) - almost every line wins, so scoring differentiates purely on card efficiency: (1) Cut Down cast at anything still on the stack (a spell hasn't resolved into a permanent yet) has no legal target and is illegal/wasted - scored low; (2) proactively casting Cut Down or Anoint with Affliction as our own root main-phase play has no good legal target on the current board except our own Vampire Token (P+T=2) or Preacher (mv3) - wasting removal on our own creatures, scored low even though we still win; (3) letting a real small threat (Floodpits Drowner 2/1=3, Deep-Cavern Bat 1/1=2, Spyglass Siren 1/1=2, Faerie Mastermind 2/1=3) resolve and then Cut Down-ing it post-resolution is clean, high-value removal; (4) Go for the Throat is unconditional so it can safely snipe Sheoldred, an animated Restless Reef, or opponent's Enduring Curiosity regardless of size - solid value; (5) casting a second legendary Kaito forces the legend rule for no gain - low value; (6) Kaito's loyalty abilities cost no mana and don't tap him (he can still attack), so they're mildly positive filler, though the -2 stun is wasted since their only creature is already tapped and it doesn't matter this turn.
response.plan: Continue holding up interaction and only firing removal at legal, resolved targets (or unconditionally with Go for the Throat); avoid wasting Cut Down/Anoint on illegal or self-owned targets. Move to combat and attack with Preacher, Vampire Token, and Kaito for lethal - opponent still has no blockers.

response.why: Same dominant position, now in Begin Combat - opponent at 1 life, no legal blockers, we have three redundant lethal attackers. Kaito loyalty abilities are no longer offered as candidates since they're sorcery-speed only and combat has begun. Scoring logic stays consistent: Cut Down at anything still on the stack (spell hasn't resolved to a permanent) is illegal/wasted - low; proactively firing Cut Down or Anoint as our own root play only has our own Vampire Token/Preacher as legal targets - wasted, low; letting a small real threat (Floodpits Drowner 2/1=3, Deep-Cavern Bat 1/1=2, Faerie Mastermind 2/1=3) resolve and then Cut Down-ing it post-resolution is clean value; Go for the Throat is unconditional so it's fine value on any real target; casting our own Enduring Curiosity or animating Restless Reef are harmless value adds since mana is abundant and the game is already won.
response.plan: Hold everything, only fire removal at legal resolved targets (or unconditionally via Go for the Throat), then proceed straight into combat and attack with Preacher, Vampire Token, and Kaito - opponent has no blockers and is at 1 life, so any unblocked attacker is lethal.

response.why: Opponent is at 1 life with their only creature tapped (cannot block) and zero cards in hand - there are no possible blockers or tricks. Attacking with everyone (attack-all) is strictly best: it guarantees lethal with maximum margin (opp_life -5), triggers Preacher's Vampire Token creation and card draw, and Enduring Curiosity draws a card for every attacker that connects - pure upside with zero risk since nothing can block or punish the attack. Holding back any single creature (Preacher, Vampire Token, or Kaito) still results in lethal since the remaining attackers alone exceed 1 life, so those lines still win but needlessly sacrifice extra card draw and margin for no benefit. Not attacking at all (attack-none) is the only genuinely bad option - it forfeits the win this turn for no reason.
response.plan: Attack with everyone - Preacher of the Schism, Vampire Token, and Kaito, Bane of Nightmares. Opponent has no blockers and is at 1 life, so this is lethal.

response.why: Attackers are already declared and tapped (Preacher, Vampire Token, Kaito) - opponent still has zero legal blockers and zero cards in hand, so combat damage is guaranteed lethal (opp at 1 life) regardless of what happens in this last priority window. Scoring differentiates only on efficiency: Cut Down/Anoint cast at a spell still on the stack has no legal target and is illegal - low; proactively firing Cut Down or Anoint as our own root play now only has our own tapped, already-attacking Vampire Token (or Preacher, mv3) as a legal target, which would actively remove our own attacking creature and reduce damage - scored lower than before for this reason; letting a small real threat (Floodpits Drowner, Spyglass Siren, Deep-Cavern Bat, Faerie Mastermind) resolve and Cut Down-ing it post-resolution is still clean value; Go for the Throat is unconditional and fine; Enduring Curiosity and animating a second Restless Reef are harmless value since they don't touch this combat's outcome.
response.plan: Hold everything and let combat proceed - opponent has no way to stop lethal damage this turn. Only use removal reactively on legal, resolved, non-own-attacker targets if something unexpected happens.

response.why: Same locked-in lethal position: attackers are declared and tapped, opponent at 1 life with no blockers and no cards in hand until they draw a Floodpits Drowner this window - still can't block since it wouldn't have vigilance-granted untapped status relevant here and combat is already committed. Scoring stays consistent: Cut Down/Anoint cast at a spell still on the stack is illegal (no permanent target yet) - low; proactively firing Cut Down/Anoint as our own root play only legally hits our own tapped attacking Vampire Token or Preacher, actively cutting our own damage - scored low; letting a small real threat (Floodpits Drowner, Deep-Cavern Bat, Faerie Mastermind) resolve then Cut Down/Go for the Throat-ing it post-resolution is clean value; Go for the Throat is unconditional and fine on any real target; our own Floodpits Drowner, Enduring Curiosity, and animating Restless Reef are all neutral value plays since they don't affect this already-locked combat.
response.plan: Hold everything and let combat proceed to lethal damage - opponent cannot stop it. Only use removal reactively on legal, resolved, non-own-attacker targets if something unexpected surfaces.

response.why: Blockers are declared (none - opponent has no legal blockers) and combat damage is now locked in for lethal - opponent at 1 life facing Preacher(2)+Vampire Token(1)+Kaito(3) unblocked. Nothing can change this outcome. Same efficiency-based scoring: Cut Down/Anoint cast at a spell still on the stack is illegal - low; proactive root Cut Down/Anoint only legally hits our own tapped attacking Vampire Token or Preacher, actively reducing our own damage for no benefit - low; letting a real small threat (Deep-Cavern Bat, Floodpits Drowner, Spyglass Siren) resolve then killing it post-resolution is clean value; Go for the Throat is fine unconditional removal; Ninjutsu is a clear misplay here - we already control Kaito, Bane of Nightmares, so bringing in a second one triggers the legend rule and requires returning one of our unblocked attackers to hand, needlessly reducing our now-lethal damage total for zero upside; Floodpits Drowner, Enduring Curiosity, and animating Restless Reef are neutral value since they don't touch this locked-in combat.
response.plan: Hold everything and let combat damage resolve for the win - it's already guaranteed. Avoid Ninjutsu (would pointlessly cut our own damage) and avoid wasting removal on our own attackers.
